text: Hi, I'm Paul, and this is Butler: an Alexa+ add-on that handles everyday stuff for you. And when you correct it, that becomes a rule the AI can't break.
It's running on an Echo Show in my simulator, talking to the real backend on AWS. The Black Box on the right logs every gateway decision.
I don't give Butler commands. I just tell it what's going on.
Tell Butler six friends from the dinner crew are coming over Friday at seven.

text: And it gets to work.
It won't interrupt me. It waits until I check in.
How's Friday looking?
It needs me to pick a cleaner. I'll go with BrightHome.
That tap goes through a separate approval path. The AI can't approve itself.
Everything it does has a receipt.
Why did you buy the drinks?
What it knew, what it turned down, and the rule that let it go ahead.
Don't buy drinks without asking me.
Yes.
The AI only picks a rule template. Regular code turns it into a policy the gateway enforces. There's the new rule.
I'm travelling Thursday to Sunday. My parents are staying at the house.
Butler tried to buy drinks for my parents, and the gateway blocked it, outside the AI, before anything was spent.
Anything you need from me?
So instead of buying, it asks me first.
What did you do this week that I might disagree with?
That's Butler, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Thanks for watching!
